title: py-sdk: credential prefetch (leaky-bucket) + streaming backpressure hints; ergonomic API + v0.20.0 bump
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduces CredentialWarmup and a leaky-bucket prefetcher to smooth auth bursts; adds streaming backpressure hint API; ergonomic convenience wrappers; bump py SDK to v0.20.0. No breaking changes, opt-in behavior. Refer to upgrade notes for migration guidance.
description:
Motivation: Large bursty workloads (e.g., chat fanout, high-concurrency embeddings) are causing auth fetch thundering and transient elevated latency/401s during cold Credential rotations. This PR adds a small, opt-in credential prefetcher using a leaky-bucket token schedule and a consumer-facing CredentialWarmup helper. It also exposes lightweight streaming backpressure hints so the SDK can signal downstream transports to slow or batch when the local leaky-bucket is drained.

Summary of changes: - core/credentials: add LeakyBucketPrefetcher (configurable rate, burst, jitter) and CredentialWarmup API. - streaming: add BackpressureHint enum and propagate hints through StreamContext so transports (http2/ws) can apply pacing. - auth: adaptive retry hooks that account for prefetched tokens. - ergonomics: convenient client.start_warmup(...) helper and retry presets (low/medium/high concurrency). - docs: usage section + migration notes. - tests: unit + integration harness exercising a simulated token endpoint and a high-concurrency streaming workload. - bump package version to 0.20.0 and add release notes.

Why leaky-bucket? A leaky-bucket prefetcher limits token fetch rate when many concurrent request paths trigger refresh simultaneously. It smooths bursts without changing token TTL semantics and is intentionally conservative (opt-in).

Developer checklist: - [x] Implement Prefetcher core and public helper. - [x] Wire backpressure hints into StreamContext. - [x] Add retry logic to prefer prefetched tokens when available. - [x] Unit tests for Prefetcher (edge cases: jitter, empty-bucket behavior). - [x] Integration tests with simulated auth server under concurrency. - [x] Docs and changelog. - [x] Version bump to 0.20.0.

Commits (high level): - 1a2b3c4: add leaky-bucket prefetcher + tests - 2b3c4d5: stream backpressure hints and plumbing into transports - 3c4d5e6: ergonomics: CredentialWarmup helper, client API surface, docs and changelog - 4d5e6f7: fix race in token handoff; adjust retry floor - 5e6f7g8: bump version, finalize release notes

Top-level changed files (illustrative): - core/credentials/prefetch.py - core/credentials/__init__.py - core/streaming/context.py - transports/http2/transport.py (apply_hint pacing) - transports/websocket/transport.py - sdk/client.py (start_warmup helper) - docs/guides/credential-prefetch.md - tests/integration/test_prefetch_concurrency.py - setup.cfg / pyproject.toml (version bump)

Testing and CI: CI run passed on first run (unit + integration on linux/py3.10, py3.11). Stress harness locally validated a 10k-rps simulated workload with backpressure hints enabled: 92% reduction in peak concurrent token fetches and elimination of 401 spikes in the harness. Bench script used is attached in tests/integration/bench_prefetch.py (small, non-blocking).

Compatibility and rollout: This is opt-in. Existing clients do not change behavior unless they call client.start_warmup(...) or configure prefetched=true in CredentialProvider. No changes to wire protocol or server-side contracts.

Documentation: docs/guides/credential-prefetch.md contains rationale, examples, and a recommended presets table. Recommend customers with bursty patterns enable warmup on client initialization: client.start_warmup(preset="high_concurrency").

Security/observability: Added metrics: sdk.auth.prefetch.attempts, sdk.auth.prefetch.successes, sdk.auth.prefetch.throttled. Also instrumented stream.hint.backpressure events so Console dashboards can correlate hints with increased latencies upstream.

Merge: Squash-merged to main. See merged_at metadata.

Known limitations and follow-ups: - Prefetcher assumes token endpoint scales; if token endpoint enforces strict per-account rate limits, operator should tune rate/burst. - Next PR: add server-side hint acceptance (server may return pacing advice to clients); tracking ENG-3490.
review_thread: Arjun Patel: Nice, this addresses a long-standing cause of auth thundering in our on-prem customers. A few nits: (1) can we make the default preset safer for low-traffic apps? (2) add an opt-out env var to disable warmup entirely?
Maya Chen: Thanks — addressed both. Default preset renamed to 'conservative' and I added REDWOOD_SDK_PREFETCH=false that disables global warmup when set. Tests updated to include env var override.

Sofia Rivera: Left comments on the transport pacing granularity; transports should not sleep more than 10ms in tight loops to avoid head-of-line issues. Also please add a doc example showing how to monitor the new metrics.
Maya Chen: Adjusted pacing in http2 transport to batch at 5-10ms windows; added doc snippet and Grafana query examples for sdk.auth.prefetch.* metrics.
Daniel Kim: Observability question: will backpressure hints inflate metric cardinality? They look low-cardinality (enum) so fine. Approving pending a small race fix in token handoff.
Maya Chen: Fixed the race (commit 4d5e6f7) and added a unit that repros the previous failure mode. Marking ready-to-merge.
Arjun Patel: Approved. CI green. Merging with squash.
